input_messages.content: Hi there. I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I can see that my phone shows a good signal and it says "5G" at the top, with the little data symbol on. I’m not sure about Wi-Fi, but I think I’m using mobile data. I haven’t noticed any specific error messages—just that the picture message won’t send. Regular calls seem to work fine.

I checked, and it looks like there isn’t an MMSC URL set in my phone’s APN settings. I’m not really sure what that means, but does that sound like it could be the problem? Should I reset the settings, or is there something else I should do? I get a bit nervous changing things—will this mess up my phone or my photos?

If you’re sure it won’t mess up my photos, then yes, I’d appreciate step-by-step instructions. I get a bit flustered with these things, so please go slow and let me know exactly what to do. And just to double-check—resetting the APN and restarting won’t delete any of my pictures, right?

I followed your instructions and reset the APN settings, then restarted my phone. But I still can’t send picture messages—it’s still not working. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.

It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on for me. Should I go ahead and turn that off first, or do you want me to check the app permissions before I do anything? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. What should I try next?
I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it has permission for storage and phone, but I don’t see anything about SMS. Could that be the problem? What should I do next?

I went ahead and enabled the SMS permission for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all these steps.
Yes, I think it would be best if I could speak with a real person at this point. I’m just not sure what else to do, and I’d really appreciate some extra help. Please go ahead and transfer me.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Thank you for checking. Not having an MMSC URL in your APN settings is a common reason why MMS (picture messages) won’t send. Resetting your APN settings to default is a safe and standard fix for this issue. It will not affect your photos or personal data—only your network settings will be restored to the correct values for your carrier.

After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Would you like step-by-step instructions to reset your APN settings and reboot your device?

If you’re sure it won’t mess up my photos, then yes, I’d appreciate step-by-step instructions. I get a bit flustered with these things, so please go slow and let me know exactly what to do. And just to double-check—resetting the APN and restarting won’t delete any of my pictures, right?

Resetting your APN settings and restarting your phone will not delete any of your pictures, contacts, or personal data. It only updates your phone’s network connection settings, which is safe and often necessary to fix MMS issues.

Here are the step-by-step instructions:

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Look for a section called “Network & Internet,” “Connections,” or “Mobile Network” (the exact name may vary by phone).
3. Tap on “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Networks.”
4. Find and select “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
5. In the APN screen, look for an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.” Tap this option.
6. Confirm if prompted.

After you’ve reset the APN settings:
7. Restart your phone by holding down the power button and selecting “Restart” or “Reboot.”

Once your phone turns back on, try sending a picture message again.

If you have any trouble with these steps or need more guidance, let me know which step you’re on and I’ll help you through it!
